newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Stocks to Watch Today - Feb 6.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Stocks to Watch Today - Feb 6.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:

News Corp announced a A$731 million net profit before abnormals for the six months to December 31, up 10.3 percent on the same period a year earlier, but below analysts expectations of a pre-abnormals net profit for the half of A$735 million to A$775 million.

Coles Myer Ltd, reported on Wednesday a firm rise in sales revenue, signalling the worst may be over for the country's struggling merchants. Coles announced a 5.4 percent rise in sales revenue to A$9.9 billion for the six months to January 26, sounding a rare note of optimism in an industry that has been hit hard by a downturn in consumer spending. It also said it expected to report a rise in annual net profit with margins widening and a solid Christmas season already under its belt.

Jupiters Ltd said late on Wednesday it expected to achieve solid revenue and profits based on strong performances from casinos in the state capital of Queensland and on the Gold Coast. The company said its operations had become increasingly competitive in the latest six months in both the premium player and local markets. Net profit in the six months to December 31, 1996 jumped to A$20.17 million from A$8.12 million a year ago.

Pasminco Ltd said on Wednesday a proposed expansion of its zinc smelter in Tasmania by about 50 percent was in jeopardy due to negotiations over additional power. Recent negotiations so far with the Hydro Electric Commission of Tasmania over supplies additional cheap power have failed to make headway John Winckel, executive general manager of metals for Pasminco told Reuters.

Newcrest Mining Ltd said gold mining activities at its Telfer gold mine in the Great Sandy Desert of Western Australia would be scaled-down for at least two weeks due to fuel supply problems caused by heavy rainfall.
